You are auditing the Nxeon hosting platform codebase at /opt/nxeon (a Next.js app). This is a READ-ONLY audit — do not edit any files.

BACKGROUND: Nxeon sells VPS and game-server hosting. Every VPS `Plan` and `GamePlan` row in the live Postgres DB has TWO price fields: `priceCents` (the regular/renewal monthly price) and `introPriceCents` (an optional LOW first-term intro price, nullable — some plans have one, and currently ALL active VPS/game plans in prod DB do have one set). `introTermMonths` is currently null for every plan, meaning null = the intro price applies to the WHOLE first term, however long that term is (not just "first month").

We discovered that ~46+ marketing landing pages under `app/(marketing)/*-server-hosting/page.tsx` (e.g. rust-server-hosting, palworld-server-hosting, ark-server-hosting, valheim-server-hosting, cs2-server-hosting, minecraft-bedrock-server-hosting, satisfactory-server-hosting, etc. — get the full list via `grep -rl "GameLandingCombined\|PREVIEW_GAMES" "app/(marketing)"` from /opt/nxeon) render pricing through `components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx` fed either by the shared HARDCODED `PREVIEW_GAMES` object in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, or by a page-local hardcoded override object (check each page — some pages define their own local `GAME` object with `plans: [{ price: "$X.XX", ... }]` instead of importing from PREVIEW_GAMES; read each page.tsx's top ~60 lines to see which). Also check the standalone hand-rolled pages `app/(marketing)/minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx` and any other `*-server-hosting/page.tsx` NOT in the GameLandingCombined list (e.g. it might use its own local `PLANS` array) — these hardcode a `PLANS` array of `{ name, price: "$X.XX", slots, blurb }` objects directly in the page file, completely disconnected from the database.

None of these hardcoded numbers are read from the DB at request time — they are point-in-time snapshots typed directly into the source, so they silently go stale whenever an admin changes a plan's price in the catalog.

YOUR TASK:
1. Get the live DB truth for every GamePlan family by running (from /opt/nxeon): a temp script via `npx tsx` importing `db` from `../lib/db` (per this repo's credential-hygiene rule — NEVER construct/print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string). Query `db.gamePlan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: [{ gameFamily: "asc" }, { priceCents: "asc" }] })` and for each row note `gameFamily`, `name`, `priceCents`, `introPriceCents`. (Delete your temp script under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` when done — do not leave it behind.)
   For reference, family codes look like: minecraft, bedrock, valheim, rust, palworld, cs2, terraria, ark, arkasa, satisfactory, projectzomboid (sdtd is 7 Days to Die), vrising, enshrouded, factorio, gmod, conan, unturned, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dst (Don't Starve Together), vintagestory, nightingale, barotrauma, corekeeper, dragonwilds, eco, empyrion, icarus, kf2 (Killing Floor 2), l4d2 (Left 4 Dead 2), mordhau, necesse, sandstorm (Insurgency Sandstorm), soulmask, spaceengineers, squad, stationeers, sunkenland, tf2, theisle, abioticfactor. Match each marketing page's game to the right family by name (e.g. rust-server-hosting -> family "rust", the-isle-server-hosting -> family "theisle", 7-days-to-die-server-hosting -> family "sdtd", ark-survival-ascended-server-hosting -> family "arkasa").

2. For every one of the ~46+ `*-server-hosting/page.tsx` pages (list them all via the grep above) PLUS `minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx` and `minecraft-bedrock-server-hosting/page.tsx` (check if that one is in the GameLandingCombined list or hand-rolled) PLUS the shared `PREVIEW_GAMES` data in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`: extract every hardcoded `price: "$X.XX"` literal you find (there are usually 2-3 tiers per game) and compare it against that family's DB `introPriceCents` values (converted to dollars) AND its `priceCents` (regular) values.

3. Classify each hardcoded price into one of:
   - MATCHES INTRO: the hardcoded number equals the current DB introPriceCents for some tier (stale-but-currently-correct — will drift the next time an admin changes the intro price, and has NO renewal disclosure at all).
   - MATCHES REGULAR: equals the DB regular priceCents.
   - MISMATCH: matches neither — genuinely wrong right now. These are the highest priority.
   - NO DB MATCH FOUND: the family/tier count doesn't line up with what's in the DB at all (e.g. game removed, family renamed, or tier count differs).

4. Produce a final report as a markdown-style table or grouped list: for each of the ~46+ pages, the file path, the family it maps to, and its classification with specific numbers (hardcoded vs DB intro vs DB regular). Call out EVERY genuine MISMATCH and NO DB MATCH FOUND case by name with exact numbers — those are the concrete, distinct "hardcoded stale price" bugs we need to report to the user. Keep the writeup for the "MATCHES INTRO" bucket brief (just list the file names) since that bucket is large and homogeneous — the point is proving the pattern, not itemizing every safe one in detail.

Also note: are there other still-hardcoded price literals anywhere else worth flagging in these same files (e.g. in `<meta>` description strings, FAQ prose, or JSON-LD) beyond the plan cards themselves? A quick scan is enough, no need to be exhaustive there.

Do NOT edit any files. Do NOT run any build or deploy commands. This is investigation only. Report back with the full findings — be concrete with file paths, line numbers where practical, and exact dollar figures for every mismatch found. This report will be relayed directly to the user, so make it self-contained and precise.

content.text:
# Nxeon Marketing Pricing Audit — Findings

## Scope covered
- **DB truth**: queried live `GamePlan` (all 37 active families) and `Plan` (4 VPS tiers) via a temporary `npx tsx` script at `scripts/_tmp-audit-prices.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db` (per the credential-hygiene rule — no raw connection strings used). **Script has been deleted** after the run.
- **Pages audited**: all 40 `*-server-hosting/page.tsx` files that render via `GameLandingCombined` + `PREVIEW_GAMES` (`components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`), plus `minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx` (hand-rolled `PLANS` array) and `fivem-server-hosting/page.tsx` (hand-rolled, sells VPS `Plan` tiers, not a `GamePlan` family). That's **42 pages** total. `singapore-dedicated-server-hosting`, `singapore-game-server-hosting`, and `vpn-server-hosting` were checked and confirmed to query `db.plan`/`db.gamePlan` live at request time — **not in scope**, no hardcoding found there.
- `introTermMonths` is `null` for every plan in prod, confirming the background's point: intro price applies to the whole (open-ended) first term with no separate "first month only" disclosure anywhere in this code.

## Headline result
Of 42 pages, **40 are internally consistent with current DB `introPriceCents`** (i.e., MATCHES INTRO — correct today, silently stale the next time an admin repriced a plan, with zero renewal-price disclosure on the page). **Only one page has a genuine live MISMATCH: `cs2-server-hosting`.** One additional MISMATCH exists in the shared data file but is currently masked on the only live page that consumes it.

---

## MISMATCH #1 (live, customer-facing) — `app/(marketing)/cs2-server-hosting/page.tsx`

Family: `cs2`. Page does `const GAME = PREVIEW_GAMES.cs2;` (line 37) with no override, so the bug lives at the source in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` lines 1166–1203 and propagates into the page's plan cards, `<meta>` description (line 26), OpenGraph description (line 32), and the `ProductOffersJsonLd` (which derives from `GAME.plans`, so it's internally consistent but equally wrong).

| Tier (data.ts id) | Hardcoded price | DB `introPriceCents` | DB `priceCents` (regular) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cs2-2` "Practice" · 2 GB | **$6.99** (line 1191) | $11.99 | $21.58 | **MISMATCH** |
| `cs2-4` "Community" · 4 GB | **$11.99** (line 1201) | $16.99 | $30.58 | **MISMATCH** |

Note the coincidence: the hardcoded 4 GB price ($11.99) equals the *2 GB* tier's real intro price — this looks like the whole CS2 price ladder shifted down one rung at some point and was never re-synced. The page's own code comment (lines 12–15) claims "already matched the PREVIEW_GAMES.cs2 demo data exactly, so no price override was needed" — true only in the sense that the page matches the (equally wrong) shared data; neither matches the DB.

## MISMATCH #2 (latent, currently masked) — shared data file `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, `PALWORLD.plans` (line 270)

`components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` line 267–270, tier `pal-16` "Full server" · 16 GB: hardcoded `price: "$24.99"`.

- DB `palworld` 16 GB tier: `introPriceCents` = **$27.99**, `priceCents` (regular) = $50.38.
- This is a real MISMATCH in the shared data object — but it does **not** currently reach a customer, because `app/(marketing)/palworld-server-hosting/page.tsx` (lines 36–40) explicitly patches around it:
  ```
  const GAME = {
    ...PREVIEW_GAMES.palworld,
    plans: PREVIEW_GAMES.palworld.plans.map((p) => (p.id === "pal-16" ? { ...p, price: "$27.99" } : p)),
  };
  ```
  So the live `palworld-server-hosting` page renders the correct $27.99 (MATCHES INTRO). The stale $24.99 is a landmine sitting in the shared file: it will render wrong on the internal `/preview/game-combined` route, and it will silently re-break `palworld-server-hosting` (or any future page) the moment anyone refactors away that inline override without noticing why it was there. Worth a code comment or a fix at the source rather than a per-page patch.

No other family showed a tier-count mismatch against the DB (i.e., no "NO DB MATCH FOUND" cases) — every family's number of hardcoded plan tiers lines up 1:1 with its DB rows, including the four families that only have 2 real tiers today (`valheim`, `terraria`, `theforest`, `sonsoftheforest`, `palworld`) and the two-tier `cs2`.

---

## MATCHES INTRO (39 of 42 pages — currently correct, no renewal price shown anywhere)

Every hardcoded `price:` on these pages equals the DB's current `introPriceCents` for its tier, and none of them equal or disclose `priceCents` (the real renewal price):

`abiotic-factor-server-hosting`, `ark-server-hosting`, `ark-survival-ascended-server-hosting`, `barotrauma-server-hosting`, `conan-exiles-server-hosting`, `core-keeper-server-hosting`, `dont-starve-together-server-hosting`, `dragonwilds-server-hosting`, `eco-server-hosting`, `empyrion-server-hosting`, `enshrouded-server-hosting`, `factorio-server-hosting`, `fivem-server-hosting` (matches VPS `Plan` intro prices, not GamePlan — Standard/Pro/Max = $12.99/$20.99/$32.99), `garrys-mod-server-hosting`, `icarus-server-hosting`, `insurgency-sandstorm-server-hosting`, `killing-floor-2-server-hosting`, `left-4-dead-2-server-hosting`, `minecraft-bedrock-server-hosting`, `minecraft-server-hosting` (hand-rolled `PLANS`, matches `minecraft` family intro), `mordhau-server-hosting`, `necesse-server-hosting`, `nightingale-server-hosting`, `palworld-server-hosting` (correct only because of its inline override, see above), `project-zomboid-server-hosting`, `rust-server-hosting`, `satisfactory-server-hosting`, `sons-of-the-forest-server-hosting`, `soulmask-server-hosting`, `space-engineers-server-hosting`, `squad-server-hosting`, `sunkenland-server-hosting`, `terraria-server-hosting`, `tf2-server-hosting`, `the-forest-server-hosting`, `the-isle-server-hosting`, `unturned-server-hosting`, `v-rising-server-hosting`, `valheim-server-hosting`, `vintage-story-server-hosting`, `7-days-to-die-server-hosting`.

All 37 corresponding entries in the shared `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` also match, except the one Palworld tier noted above.

## Other hardcoded price literals checked (beyond plan cards)

- Every page's `<meta name="description">` and OpenGraph description repeats the same "From $X.XX/mo" figure as the page's lowest plan-card tier — so these track (or mis-track) in lockstep with the plan cards; no independent drift found. (This means CS2's meta/OG descriptions are also wrong, quoting $6.99/mo.)
- `ProductOffersJsonLd` blocks are computed programmatically from `GAME.plans` (`price: parseFloat(p.price...)`), not separately hardcoded — so JSON-LD is never a second source of drift, it just inherits whatever the plan cards say (right or wrong).
- FAQ prose on pages with more `$` literals (e.g. `v-rising`, `project-zomboid`, `unturned`, `garrys-mod`, `7-days-to-die`, `factorio`, `satisfactory`) only restates the same already-correct tier prices in sentences like "The 8 GB plan at $15.00…" — no separate stale numbers found there. Several files also carry price figures inside `/* code comments */` documenting the old pre-GamePlan VPS-tier pricing (e.g. gmod/unturned mention "$12.99/$20.99/$32.99 — no longer applied") — these are non-rendered developer notes, not customer-facing, but confirm the pattern of prices being typed in by hand at authoring time with no live binding.

## Bottom line

The stale-hardcoding risk described in the background is real and systemic (39 of 42 pages have zero connection to the DB and would silently go wrong on any repricing), but as of **today** only **two concrete numeric bugs** exist:
1. `cs2-server-hosting` (and its root cause, `PREVIEW_GAMES.cs2` in `data.ts`) — both tiers wrong: $6.99 should be $11.99, $11.99 should be $16.99.
2. `PREVIEW_GAMES.palworld` `pal-16` in `data.ts` line 270 — $24.99 should be $27.99 (masked on the live page by a manual override, but landmine for the preview route and any future refactor).

Separately worth flagging to the user: none of these 42 pages disclose a renewal price at all — every "MATCHES INTRO" page advertises only the intro price with no "then $X renewal" copy, and since `introTermMonths` is null (whole first term, not "first month"), that gap is arguably a bigger customer-trust issue than the two numeric mismatches, though it's a design/copy question rather than a "wrong number" bug.
